claims.text: At stage-1 no test in OrderServiceTests cancels a `shipped` order (comment at the end of the class); with public setters a test could seed an order with Status = "shipped" and would need a FakeOrderRepository, a FakeNotifier, an OrderService and an await on CancelOrderAsync.

At stage-2 the rule lives in Order.Cancel(): a `shipped` order makes it throw OrderStatusException with Code "already-shipped"; the test project has DonHang.Tests/Domain/OrderTests.cs next to Services/OrderServiceTests.cs.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs:83-88; DonHang.Domain/OrderStatusException.cs; git ls-tree stage-2 DonHang.Tests

claims.text: OrderTests creates each order through the helper NewOrder(), which calls the public constructor with one item (OneItem()); no test in the class uses a repository, a notifier, a fake or await; every test method returns void.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Tests/Domain/OrderTests.cs:6-13 and whole file

claims.text: After creation only MarkPaid() (from new), Ship() (from paid) and Cancel() (from new or paid) change Status; they are synchronous void methods, and Order calls no repository or notifier (no dependency a fake could stand in for).

Status has a private setter at stage-2, so a test reaches `shipped` only by calling MarkPaid() then Ship() (Ship() accepts only a paid order); no endpoint takes payments at stage-2 and MarkPaid() is called only from OrderTests.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: Entities.cs:35,72-80; git grep MarkPaid stage-2

claims.text: Cancel_ShippedOrder_Throws (OrderTests.cs:38-51) calls MarkPaid(), Ship(), then Assert.Throws<OrderStatusException>(order.Cancel), asserts ex.Code == "already-shipped" and order.Status == "shipped". OrderStatusException is what Order throws for a disallowed change; Code names the case.

xUnit's Assert.Throws<T>(Action) accepts a method group such as order.Cancel, invokes it itself, fails when no T is thrown, and returns the exception; Assert.Single(collection) fails unless the collection has exactly one element and returns it.
claims.source_hint: xUnit v2 Assert.Throws<T>(Action), Assert.Single (xunit.assert); verified by execution

claims.text: At stage-2 OrderServiceTests has six tests: three for PlaceOrderAsync; CancelOrderAsync_NewOrder_SavesAndNotifies (order cancelled in the fake repository, one notification); CancelOrderAsync_UnknownOrder_Throws; ShipOrderAsync_NewOrder_ThrowsAndNotifiesNobody. OneItem() returns a one-item list.
No test in OrderServiceTests at stage-2 checks whether a `shipped` order may be cancelled.

A rule inside the entity is cheaper to test than the same rule inside a service, because the test creates only the object under test instead of wiring its dependencies; repeating each status rule in OrderServiceTests would duplicate OrderTests with more setup.
A fake stands in for a dependency; a class with no dependency, such as Order, needs none in its tests.
`dotnet test DonHang.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~DonHang.Tests.Domain"` runs only tests whose fully qualified name contains that text (the ~ operator means contains).

In a stage-2 checkout: the Domain filter runs 10 tests, all pass; after deleting the `Status == "shipped"` throw in Cancel(), only Cancel_ShippedOrder_Throws fails (9 pass); the OrderServiceTests filter then runs 6 tests, all pass.
